images.caption: Figure 1:Top.Comparison of scene representations for indoor scene generation. Object sequences (a) encode object attributes but lack explicit spatial relationship information. Semantic maps (b) make spatial structure explicit, but lack vertical, instance, and orientation information. We propose RoomTokens (c) to address these missing factors by encoding semantic occupancy, instance identity, and facing cues in a sliced spatial grid.Bottom.We introduceMDiRT(d), a masked discrete diffusion model over RoomTokens, which denoises missing token fields while keeping architectural tokens fixed so generated scenes respect room boundaries.

Figure 2:RoomToken data representation. (a) A 3D scene is represented as horizontal slices taken at selected vertical heights. (b) Each slice encodes three aligned 2D channels: semantic class, instance-color identity, and the facing field. Stacking these channels over all heights forms a sliced token volume. (c) The resulting 3D representation of stacked slices (RoomTokens) stores semantic, instance, and orientation information, with height derived from the slice index.

Figure 3:Overview ofMDiRT. Given selected height slices and an architectural mask, we clamp the fixed room structure and denoise masked interior RoomTokens with a shared UNet with cross-slice attention. The denoiser predicts semantic, instance-color, and facing slices under semantic-gated validity constraints: architecture/background tokens carry no instance-color or facing cues, while furniture tokens do. The valid RoomToken grid is then grouped into object records, whose category, size, and pose are used to retrieve and place matched 3D assets.

Figure 4:Arch-mask-conditioned qualitative comparison on 3D-FRONT. We use semantic orthographic views to focus the comparison on layout evaluation. Baselines show boundary violations, collisions, or blocked door/window openings, whileMDiRTpreserves clear openings, room geometry, and structured object cues.
Figure 5:Failure cases: implausible layouts (green), object intersections (orange), and blocked doorways (blue).
